lesson_title: The Price Tag Behind the Price Tag: Scarcity and Opportunity Cost
hook_text: Everything you buy has TWO price tags. You only ever read one.
clip_script: Every choice wears two price tags. The first is printed: R120 for the calculator. The second is invisible and heavier: what ELSE that R120 would have been. Your genuine second choice was the data bundle — so the TRUE cost of the calculator is one data bundle. Not R120. The money left your pocket either way; the bundle is what you'll actually live without. Economists call it opportunity cost, and once you see it, you can't unsee it. The Saturday shift pays R150 — but in exam season its hidden tag reads 'one day of matric revision', and that tag can cost more than the money earns. Even FREE things carry it: the free event still costs the afternoon, and the afternoon had a next-best use. That's the rule: the true price of anything is the next-best thing you give up. Money measures the front of the tag. Life is lived on the back of it.
visual_style: Price tags flipping in slow motion to reveal glowing hidden sides — a calculator's tag flipping to show a data bundle, a payslip flipping to show a study desk, a 'FREE' sticker flipping to show a clock.
pacing: Steady tag-flip rhythm, each flip landing a beat harder, closing on the front/back line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start reading both tags.
